transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um, yeah… thanks for seeing me. I guess what brought me in is that the things that normally make me feel like me—going out for photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar clean and organized—started feeling kind of flat. Heavy, I guess.

It’s not like I can’t do anything, exactly, but I’ve just stopped initiating those things the way I used to. I kept telling myself it was just being busy or tired, but… it felt worth checking on. Does that make sense?
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Yeah, I mean… I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but it did seem to start after some changes with a family member’s health and behavior. I ended up taking on more of the coordinating—appointments, checking in, keeping things straight.

It’s been going on maybe about a year and three months now. I kept thinking I was just adjusting to the extra responsibility, you know? Does that sound like the kind of thing you mean?
During this time, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most days, exactly. I’ve had days where I feel kind of low or weighed down, but I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

It’s more like things have felt… muted, maybe? But if you mean really down all day nearly every day, I don’t know that I’d say that. Is that a fair distinction?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge a lot of the time?

Um… anxious, maybe a little, but I wouldn’t say a lot of the time. Not like I’m constantly on edge or anything.

I do get tense when there’s a lot to manage, or when I feel like I’m not keeping up the way I should, but I’ve kind of assumed that’s normal stress. I don’t know if that counts as anxiety the way you mean it.
During this past year, was there ever a two-week period when you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t think so… not a full two weeks like that. I’ve had stretches where I felt kind of low or tired of everything, but “most of the day nearly every day” sounds stronger than what I remember.

I mean, I might be underplaying it a little, but I don’t want to say yes if it wasn’t really that. Does that make sense?
When you notice this heaviness or flatness, does it feel mainly connected to what’s been going on with your family member?

Maybe partly, yeah. I mean, the family stuff probably doesn’t help.

But… it wasn’t only that, I don’t think. What actually made me come in was more that things that usually make me feel like myself started feeling kind of flat and heavy. Like going out for photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar clean and organized… I just stopped initiating those things.

Not because I was trying to be difficult or anything. It just felt harder to start, and less… rewarding, I guess. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you actually lost interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t say I don’t care about anything, exactly, but the things that usually make me feel like myself have started feeling kind of flat.

Like my photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar clean and organized… I stopped initiating them. It’s not that I hate them or anything. They just feel heavier to start, and not as rewarding once I do. Is that what you mean by losing interest or pleasure?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I do feel worn down sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it unusually tired.

It’s more like… things take a little more effort than they should, maybe. But I’m still getting through the day, so I don’t want to overstate it. Does that count as low energy, or are you asking more like physically exhausted?
Have you had trouble sleeping, or been sleeping more than usual?

A little, yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I’m not up all night every night.

But there have been nights where I only sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I’m awake before dawn. And weirdly I don’t always feel tired right away — I’ll feel like I should answer emails or update appointment lists or get things organized.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of sleep trouble you mean?
When you sleep only two or three hours, do you still feel rested the next day?

Sometimes, yes… which is the part that feels a little odd.

Like, I’ll only get two or three hours, wake up before dawn, and instead of feeling wiped out right away, I’ll feel ready to answer emails or update appointment lists. I know that probably isn’t ideal, but in the moment it feels like I’m rested enough to get going.
During those times when you slept only a few hours and still felt ready to go, did you also feel unusually upbeat or energized?

Yeah… I think so, at times. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m bouncing off the walls or anything, but I’ll have stretches where I feel really upbeat, like everything is clicking and I’m on top of things.

And then… sometimes it flips kind of fast. Like if someone moves a meeting or changes something small, I can get sharper with people than I meant to be. Not yelling, usually, just… more clipped or irritated than feels like me afterward. Does that make sense?
Have those more upbeat, needing-less-sleep periods ever lasted at least 4 days in a row?

Yeah… I think they have. I was trying not to make too much of it, but those kinds of stretches have been happening on and off for, I guess, about eleven months now.

Not nonstop the whole time, but recurring — where I’m sleeping less, feeling more driven, more confident than usual. And some of those periods have definitely gone several days in a row, at least four days, I’d say.
During those stretches when you sleep less and feel more upbeat, do you find yourself taking on more projects or getting much more done than usual?

Yes… I do. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just being productive, and some of it is useful. But during those stretches I’ll start rebuilding work templates, making care plans, emailing relatives, reorganizing files… kind of all at once.

It’s like sitting still feels wrong, like if I’m not doing something, I’m dropping the ball. I don’t know if that counts as “much more,” but it’s definitely more than my usual pace.
During those more upbeat periods, have they ever caused serious problems in your life—like getting you into major trouble at work or home, or leading to hospitalization?

No, not like… hospitalization or anything major like that. I’ve kept working, and overall my job has stayed intact.

I guess the honest version is there have been some smaller problems. I’ve missed calendar details that I normally wouldn’t miss, and I’ve had to double-check things that used to feel automatic. That bothers me, but I don’t think it’s gotten me into major trouble.

Outside of work, I’ve pulled back some from photography outings and mentoring because I don’t feel as present or reliable. I don’t know if that counts as serious impairment, but it’s not nothing, I guess.
